post.description:
Bourdet derivative dΔp/d(ln Δt) in flowing (drawdown) time.

Parameters
----------
dt : array_like
    Elapsed time since the rate change, any time unit (> 0, strictly increasing;
    duplicates are refused). The derivative is independent of the time unit.
dp : array_like
    Pressure change Δp, ``pressure_unit``; same length as ``dt`` (>= 3 points).
window_ln : float
    Smoothing distance L in natural-log units of time (> 0). L = 0 is not allowed;
    the smallest L that still selects neighbours is any value below the minimum
    log-spacing.
sigma_p : float
    Standard deviation of the independent pressure error per point, ``pressure_unit``
    (>= 0), propagated linearly to the derivative.
pressure_unit : {"Pa", "kPa", "MPa", "psi", "bar"}

Returns
-------
CalculationRecord
    ``derivative`` (``pressure_unit``), ``sigma_derivative`` (``pressure_unit``) and
    ``side`` (0 = central, −1 = backward only, +1 = forward only).

Raises
------
InputValidationError
    Non-finite values, < 3 points, non-positive or non-increasing time, L <= 0,
    sigma_p < 0, unknown unit.
NumericalError
    Some point has no neighbour at distance >= L on either side (record shorter than L).

Notes
-----
Maturity: M2. Exact for Δp linear in ln t; for Δp ∝ t with uniform log spacing equal
to L it returns Δp·sinh(L)/L (smoothing bias L²/6, tested). Assumptions: A-008, A-016.

post.description:
Fit qi, Di, b of a pure Arps hyperbola by bounded nonlinear least squares.

Residuals are ``ln q_model − ln q_obs`` on the included points (A-013), solved with
``scipy.optimize.least_squares`` (trust-region reflective) with bounds qi > 0,
Di > 0, 0 <= b <= 2.

Parameters
----------
t : array_like
    Time in ``time_unit`` (>= 0, strictly increasing).
q : array_like
    Observed rate (any unit), same length as ``t``.
include : array_like of bool
    Explicit mask of points used in the fit (shut-ins and outliers must be excluded
    here). Included points must have q > 0.
time_unit : {"day", "month", "year"}

Returns
-------
CalculationRecord
    ``qi``, ``di``, ``b`` and their standard errors ``*_se`` (from the Jacobian,
    s²·(JᵀJ)⁻¹), ``rmse`` and ``r2`` (in rate space, included points), ``converged``
    (1/0), ``nfev``, ``n_points`` and ``q_fitted`` (evaluated at all t, including
    excluded points, for diagnostics).

Raises
------
InputValidationError
    Bad shapes, non-bool mask, included q <= 0, t not strictly increasing.
IdentifiabilityError
    Fewer than 4 included points, or ill-conditioned Jacobian (cond > 1e12).

Notes
-----
Maturity: M2 — recovers parameters of exact and noisy synthetic curves (seeded).
Assumptions: A-008, A-010, A-011, A-013.

post.description:
Effective decline over one period from the nominal decline per that period.

b = 0 gives the (tangent) effective decline ``1 − exp(−D)``; b > 0 gives the
**secant** effective decline ``1 − (1 + b·D)^(−1/b)`` (SPEE REP #6), i.e.
``1 − q(1 period)/qi`` for an Arps hyperbola.

Parameters
----------
d_nominal : array_like
    Nominal decline per period (> 0, fraction, e.g. 0.30 for 30 %/period).
b : float
    Hyperbolic exponent in [0, 2].

Returns
-------
CalculationRecord
    ``d_effective`` (fraction per period).

Notes
-----
Maturity: M3 — reproduces SPEE REP #6 Table 1 (VAL-DCA-L01). Assumptions: A-008, A-011.

post.description:
Find **all** intersections of IPR and TPR on their common rate range.

f(q) = pwf_IPR(q) − pwf_TPR(q) is sampled on a uniform grid of ``n_grid`` points over
[max(q_min_TPR, 0), min(q_max_TPR, q_max_IPR)]; each sign change is refined with
Brent's method (``xtol``, ``maxiter``). An intersection is **stable** when
df/dq < 0 there (a small rate increase makes the tubing need more pressure than the
reservoir supplies), otherwise unstable.

Parameters
----------
ipr : IPRModel
    :class:`LinearIPR`, :class:`VogelIPR` or :class:`CompositeIPR`.
tpr : TPRModel
    :class:`TabulatedTPR`.
pressure_unit : {"Pa", "kPa", "MPa", "psi", "bar"}
    Common unit of IPR and TPR pressures (recorded).
n_grid : int
    Grid points for bracketing (>= 10). Intersections closer than one grid step can
    be missed; a near-tangency raises a warning.
xtol : float
    Absolute rate tolerance for Brent's method (> 0).
maxiter : int
    Maximum Brent iterations (>= 1).

Returns
-------
CalculationRecord
    ``q_op``, ``pwf_op`` and ``stable`` (1/0) arrays (possibly empty) and
    ``n_solutions``. Warnings: ``NO_INTERSECTION``, ``POSSIBLE_TANGENCY``,
    ``MULTIPLE_SOLUTIONS``.

Raises
------
InputValidationError
    Bad numerical settings or no overlapping rate range.
NumericalError
    Brent's method failed to converge.

Notes
-----
Maturity: M2. Assumptions: A-014, A-015.

azimuth_deg : array_like, shape (n,)
    Azimuth in degrees from North, clockwise; any finite value (normalised to [0, 360)).
length_unit : {"m", "ft"}
    Unit of ``md`` and of the start coordinates.
azimuth_reference : {"true", "magnetic", "grid"}
    Declared reference of ``azimuth_deg``. Recorded only; no correction applied (A-002).
start_east, start_north, start_tvd : float
    Coordinates of the first station, in ``length_unit``.

Returns
-------
CalculationRecord
    Station arrays (length n): ``md_m``, ``north_m``, ``east_m``, ``tvd_m``,
    ``horizontal_displacement_m``, ``closure_azimuth_deg``.
    Interval arrays (length n−1, interval i is between stations i and i+1):
    ``delta_north_m``, ``delta_east_m``, ``delta_tvd_m``, ``dogleg_deg``,
    ``dls_deg_per_30m``, ``dls_deg_per_100ft``.

Raises
------
InputValidationError
    Non-finite values, mismatched lengths, n < 2, MD not strictly increasing,
    inclination outside [0, 180], unsupported unit or reference.
PhysicalConsistencyError
    A course has a dogleg ≥ π − 1e-6 rad (reversal: the arc is undefined).

Notes
-----
Maturity: M3 — reproduces a published build example (Bourgoyne et al. 1991, as
tabulated by Amorin & Broni-Bediako 2010) within its 0.01 ft rounding (VAL-WP-L01).

Assumptions: A-001, A-002, A-003, A-004, A-005, A-008.

The method is exact for circular arcs between stations.

References
----------
Sawaryn & Thorogood (2005), SPE-84246-PA.
